Theme: Caregiving coordinates a differentiated care network
Organizing concept: Caregivers connect interpretation, supply, reminding, checking, and clinical consultation while older adults may retain taking.
Sub-theme: Responsibility follows presence and may settle without a formal decision
What it means: Whoever is available may remind or notice a low supply.
Boundary and variation: Gradual role acquisition is directly supported by one caregiver and is not generalized.

Theme: Caregiving coordinates a differentiated care network
Organizing concept: Caregivers connect interpretation, supply, reminding, checking, and clinical consultation while older adults may retain taking.
Sub-theme: Knowledge and authority sit with different people
What it means: Caregivers may hold papers and names, pharmacists interpret handwriting, and doctors authorize changes.
Boundary and variation: Collective decision making is structured rather than interchangeable.

Theme: Caregiving coordinates a differentiated care network
Organizing concept: Caregivers connect interpretation, supply, reminding, checking, and clinical consultation while older adults may retain taking.
Sub-theme: Support does not erase older adult participation
What it means: Caregiver coordination can leave recognition and taking with the older adult.
Boundary and variation: Family involvement is not automatic evidence of dependence.

Theme: Distance and transition turn coordination into uncertain verification
Organizing concept: Work, travel, and changed routines separate the people and cues that normally align medication work.
What it means: When everyone is occupied, responsibility does not move cleanly to another person.
Boundary and variation: A collective lapse is not proof that one family member failed to care.

Theme: Distance and transition turn coordination into uncertain verification
Organizing concept: Work, travel, and changed routines separate the people and cues that normally align medication work.
Sub-theme: Distance converts observation into trust and contact
What it means: Caregivers away from home call or rely on verbal confirmation.
Boundary and variation: An unobserved dose is uncertain rather than necessarily missed.

Theme: Distance and transition turn coordination into uncertain verification
Organizing concept: Work, travel, and changed routines separate the people and cues that normally align medication work.
Sub-theme: Checking carries care and pressure together
What it means: Checking can reassure caregivers while repeated questions may irritate older adults.
Boundary and variation: Monitoring cannot be classified in advance as care or surveillance.

Theme: Current tools solve isolated tasks but do not coordinate handoffs
Organizing concept: Existing aids have variable fit because they may shift work or leave interpretation to another person.
Sub-theme: An aid can redistribute maintenance work
What it means: A pillbox may create a new refilling task.
Boundary and variation: Pillbox abandonment comes from one household.

Theme: Current tools solve isolated tasks but do not coordinate handoffs
Organizing concept: Existing aids have variable fit because they may shift work or leave interpretation to another person.
Sub-theme: Signals without medicine meaning leave family interpretation
What it means: A generic alarm may indicate time without specifying medicine or relation to food.
Boundary and variation: The problem is missing meaning rather than sound itself.

Theme: Current tools solve isolated tasks but do not coordinate handoffs
Organizing concept: Existing aids have variable fit because they may shift work or leave interpretation to another person.
Sub-theme: Low technology practices remain legitimate baselines
What it means: Paper prescriptions and ordinary alarms already suffice in one caregiver account.
Boundary and variation: Future technology must exceed the value of situated current practices.

Theme: Future technology should support selective coordination under human authority
Organizing concept: Caregivers connect proposed features to current breakdowns while retaining human verification and clinical authority.
Sub-theme: Prompts should specify the medicine action
What it means: Speech, names, timing, and visual matching make a reminder actionable.
Boundary and variation: These are elicited expectations rather than reports of use.
RQ and contribution: RQ1 with formative support for RQ3; C3 basis

Theme: Future technology should support selective coordination under human authority
Organizing concept: Caregivers connect proposed features to current breakdowns while retaining human verification and clinical authority.
Sub-theme: Escalation should wait, remain selective, and be visible
What it means: Another reminder and time to respond should precede an exception alert to one caregiver.
Boundary and variation: A missing confirmation cannot prove a missed dose.
RQ and contribution: RQ1 with formative support for RQ3; C3 basis

Theme: Future technology should support selective coordination under human authority
Organizing concept: Caregivers connect proposed features to current breakdowns while retaining human verification and clinical authority.
Sub-theme: Kin may configure while clinicians decide
What it means: Trusted kin may enter schedules, but medication changes remain with clinicians.
Boundary and variation: Delegated setup still requires visibility and revocability.
RQ and contribution: RQ1 with formative support for RQ3; C3 basis
